subject: Vocabulary
description: High-hit antonym pairs from SSC/banking PYQ; common confusion clusters

questions.explanation: TRANSPARENT = clear; allows light to pass; honest, open. ANTONYM = OPAQUE = blocking light, not see-through; (figurative) hard to understand, hidden. Translucent (partially see-through, e.g., frosted glass) is BETWEEN transparent + opaque. Common figurative use: 'transparent governance' vs 'opaque dealings'. SSC PYQ word.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.explanation: LACONIC = using few words; concise to the point of curtness. (From SPARTANS — natives of Laconia, Greece — famously brief in speech. When Philip II of Macedon threatened 'If I invade Lakonia, I will raze your city', Spartans replied just 'IF'.) ANTONYM = VERBOSE = wordy, long-winded. Other antonyms: garrulous, loquacious, prolix. Synonyms of laconic: terse, brief, succinct, pithy, curt.

options.option_text: Permanent, lasting for very long time

questions.explanation: EPHEMERAL (Greek 'ephemeros' = lasting one day) = short-lived, fleeting, transient. 'Ephemeral fame', 'ephemeral beauty of cherry blossoms'. ANTONYM = PERMANENT, eternal, enduring, perpetual, everlasting. Synonyms of ephemeral: fleeting, transient, transitory, momentary, evanescent, short-lived. Common SSC PYQ word.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.explanation: GREGARIOUS (Latin 'grex' = flock) = fond of company, sociable; (zoology) living in flocks/herds. People who enjoy social gatherings + lots of friends are gregarious. ANTONYM = SOLITARY, reclusive, antisocial, introverted, withdrawn. Note: 'gregarious' is positive; 'antisocial' is negative — but a SOLITARY person is not necessarily antisocial.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

options.option_text: Brief, lasting a short time only

questions.explanation: PROLIFIC = producing in large quantities (offspring, books, work, ideas). 'Prolific writer' = writes many books. (From Latin 'proles' = offspring + 'facere' = make.) ANTONYM = BARREN, sterile, fruitless, unproductive. Synonyms of prolific: productive, fertile, fecund, profuse. Common SSC + banking word.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.explanation: AUDACIOUS = bold, daring, fearless; sometimes recklessly so. (From Latin 'audax' = bold.) Can be positive ('audacious goal') or slightly negative ('audacious lie' = brazen). ANTONYM = TIMID, cowardly, fearful, cautious, fainthearted. Synonyms: bold, daring, brave, intrepid, fearless, plucky, valiant.

options.option_text: Outdated, no longer in any use
Ancient, very old in age and date
Unique, one of a special kind only

questions.explanation: OBSOLETE = no longer in use, outdated, replaced. 'Floppy disks are obsolete'. ANTONYM = MODERN, current, contemporary, up-to-date, latest, in vogue. Synonyms of obsolete: archaic, antiquated, outdated, defunct, passé, redundant. Note 'archaic' = very old, often deliberately retained in some contexts; 'obsolete' = simply no longer used.
